chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: When the news of the raid of Mu'awiyah's men on al-Anbar reached him, he himself went out walking until he reached an-Nukhaylah, and the people overtook him and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, we are sufficient for them.'

key_terms.الْأَنْبَارِ: al-Anbar, a strategic town in Iraq
key_terms.نَكْفِيكَهُمْ: we will suffice you against them (handle the fighting)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do when he heard about Muawiyah's attack on al-Anbar?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) humility and readiness to lead from the front during the Battle of the Camel, specifically when Mu'awiyah’s forces raided al-Anbar. His refusal to let his companions carry him or take over the command underscores his personal involvement in the conflict and his rejection of the aristocratic norms of the time. This event serves as a poignant example of his leadership style, contrasting his ascetic approach with the political maneuvering of his rivals.
